sn11.12:1.2: There the Blessed One said to the bhikkhus:
sn11.12:1.3: “Bhikkhus, in the past, when Sakka, lord of the devas, was a human being, he was a brahmin youth named Magha; therefore he is called Maghavā.
sn11.12:2.1: Bhikkhus, in the past, when Sakka, lord of the devas, was a human being, he gave gifts in city after city; therefore he is called Purindada, the Urban Giver.
sn11.12:3.1: Bhikkhus, in the past, when Sakka, lord of the devas, was a human being, he gave gifts considerately; therefore he is called Sakka.
sn11.12:4.1: Bhikkhus, in the past, when Sakka, lord of the devas, was a human being, he gave a rest house; therefore he is called Vāsava.
sn11.12:5.1: Bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, thinks of a thousand matters in a moment; therefore he is called Sahassakkha, Thousand-eyed.
sn11.12:6.1: Bhikkhus, Sakka's wife is the asura maiden named Sujā; therefore he is called Sujampati, Sujā's husband.
sn11.12:7.1: Bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, exercises supreme sovereignty and rulership over the Tavatimsa devas; therefore he is called lord of the devas.
sn11.12:8.1: Bhikkhus, in the past, when Sakka, lord of the devas, was a human being, he adopted and undertook seven vows by the undertaking of which he achieved the status of Sakka.
sn11.12:8.3: ‘As long as I live may I support my parents.’
sn11.12:8.4: ‘As long as I live may I respect the family elders.’
sn11.12:8.5: ‘As long as I live may I speak gently.’
sn11.12:8.6: ‘As long as I live may I not speak divisively.’
sn11.12:8.7: ‘As long as I live may I dwell at home with a mind devoid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, delighting in relinquishment, devoted to charity, delighting in giving and sharing.’
sn11.12:8.8: ‘As long as I live may I speak the truth.’
sn11.12:8.9: ‘As long as I live may I be free from anger, and if anger should arise in me may I dispel it quickly.’
sn11.12:8.10: In the past, bhikkhus, when Sakka, lord of the devas, was a human being, he adopted and undertook these seven vows by the undertaking of which he achieved the status of Sakka.
sn11.12:9.1: When a person supports his parents,
sn11.12:9.3: When his speech is gentle and courteous,
sn11.12:9.4: And he refrains from divisive words;
sn11.12:10.1: When he strives to remove meanness,
